title: variantly.tools — choose the page structure (round 2)
question: Earlier structures are out (no check-in pass, board or keep sections). All three lead with the before/after of real Impeccable redesigns, keep the human/agent fork, and show the stacks with logos. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Flip Headline
options.thesis: The page cycles itself: the headline is a split-flap line that flips through the variants' directions while the before/after beneath swaps in sync, so the first viewport shows six redesigns without a click.
options.viewport: Header with fork. A one-line flap headline (e.g. 'Oak & Iron, as EDITORIAL'). Under it, nearly full-viewport, the live before/after; the flap and the right pane change together every few seconds; hover or 1–6 takes control. Install chip at the bottom edge.
options.risk: Auto-cycling can feel like a carousel; it must stop the moment you touch anything.

regions.label: flap headline: Oak & Iron, as EDITORIAL
how it works · stacks with logos

options.label: Compare Is the Hero
options.thesis: No preamble: the first viewport is the before/after itself, full-bleed, with the headline and install sitting on it as small board tags, exactly like the app's own compare view.
options.viewport: Edge-to-edge before/after of Oak & Iron; top-left tag 'N redesigns. Keep one.'; bottom dock with 1–6, the install chip and Keep; scroll down for the short story, stacks and install.
options.risk: Visitors who don't drag may not grasp it's interactive; the grip and dock must say so.

regions.label: fork as a small tag row

options.label: Diptych Spreads
options.thesis: A catalogue of transformations: after a short hero, each variant gets its own spread, original and redesign side by side at the same scroll, with what changed listed in the margin.
options.viewport: Headline and install on the left, the first spread (original | V01 Editorial) already on the right; each scroll step is the next spread.
options.risk: Six spreads is a long page; the compare becomes passive viewing instead of a tool you play with.
